checked.found: Opened Wikipedia: Zemsky Sobor elected Michael in 1613 (21 Feb OS) at about age 16. That page does not list the delegates; a search of the Zemsky Sobor of 1613 results describes delegates from the nobility, clergy, merchants and townsmen.

Opened Wikipedia: Ivan (16) and Peter (10) crowned joint tsars 25 June 1682 after the streltsy Moscow Uprising; Sophia, Ivan's full sister and Peter's half-sister, was regent. Ivan and Peter were half-brothers. The streltsy were Moscow's musketeer corps rather than strictly palace guards, but this is close enough.

Opened Wikipedia: Grand Embassy ran 9 March 1697 to 25 Aug 1698; Peter travelled as 'Peter Mikhailov' and worked incognito at Dutch shipyards and in English dockyards at Deptford. Start year 1697 matches.
Opened Wikipedia: founded 27 May 1703 by Peter on swampy ground; a Baltic seaport traditionally called the Window to the West.

The prlib.ru page would not load for me (browser check), but its search snippet and other search results agree. The Senate and Synod asked Peter to take the title of Emperor on 22 Oct (OS) 1721, alongside the celebration of the Treaty of Nystad, which ended the war with Sweden. One result mentions the Senate deciding in September 1721, still 1721.

Opened Wikipedia: coup on the night of 25 Nov (OS) / 6 Dec 1741, backed by the Preobrazhensky Guards, bloodless, deposing infant Ivan VI and the regency of Anna Leopoldovna. The page notes unpopular German advisers (Osterman, Munnich) were exiled afterwards, which supports 'German-influenced'.
Opened Wikipedia: Catherine annexed the Crimean Khanate 19 April 1783; Akhtiar (Sevastopol) was chosen as a warm-water port and later housed the Black Sea Fleet.

Opened Wikipedia: Paul killed in his bedroom at St Michael's Castle, night of 23 March (OS 11 March) 1801; his son Alexander I succeeded. 'Unpopular' is not confirmed on the part of the page I read, but it is a standard characterisation.
Opened Wikipedia: 26 Dec (OS 14 Dec) 1825, Senate Square; Guards officers and about 3,000 troops refused to swear to Nicholas I and were crushed by loyalist artillery.

Opened Wikipedia: officially opened 30 Oct 1837; the first public railway in the Russian Empire, steam-hauled, carrying mostly passengers, about 27 km from St Petersburg to Pavlovsk via Tsarskoye Selo. Tests in 1836. The name says 'Russia's First Railway', which is slightly loose (first public line), but the year is right.
Opened Wikipedia: serialised in The Russian Messenger 1865-1867; the complete book was published in 1869.
Opened Wikipedia: the first Imperial egg was the Hen Egg of 1885, with a golden hen inside; Alexander III gave it to Empress Maria Feodorovna and ordered one every Easter after that.

Opened Wikipedia: infobox says work began 1891, with termini at Moscow and Vladivostok. The page text I read did not mention the first stone. A search found several sources saying Tsarevich Nicholas laid the first stone at Vladivostok on 31 May 1891; I did not open those pages.
Opened Wikipedia: became emperor 1 Nov 1894 when Alexander III died at 49; abdicated in 1917, ending the Romanov dynasty.
Opened World History Encyclopedia: 22 Jan 1905, soldiers fired on peaceful workers marching to petition Nicholas II, helping spark the 1905 Revolution.

Opened Wikipedia: Russia mobilised 30 July 1914 in support of Serbia; Germany declared war on 1 Aug and Austria-Hungary on 6 Aug. Strictly Germany declared war on Russia, but the description's wording is acceptable.

Opened History.com: killed 29-30 Dec 1916 by nobles led by Yusupov and Grand Duke Dmitri; cyanide-laced food, shot, thrown into a river; he had great influence over the czarina and Nicholas II. The poison, shooting and drowning account is the traditional one and is disputed by modern historians.
